author: HarishSV01
title: Harmonic Mean : F1-score is the harmonic mean of Precision and Recall because it penalizes a large imbalance between them.
body:
**F1-score is the harmonic mean of Precision and Recall because it penalizes a large imbalance between them.**

The Harmonic Mean is used when dealing with rates, such as:

Speed
Price per unit
Cost per item
Ratios
Performance metrics like the F1-score in Machine Learning

**Formula
HM = n / (1/x₁ + 1/x₂ + ... + 1/xₙ)**

Most Famous Example

Suppose you travel:

**First half of the distance at 60 km/hr
Second half of the distance at 40 km/hr**

Many people **incorrectly calculate:
**
(60 + 40)/2 = 50 km/hr

But the **correct average** speed is the Harmonic Mean:

**HM = 2 / (1/60 + 1/40)
   = 48 km/hr**

So:
Average speed = 48 km/hr
not 50 km/hr.


**Case 1: Equal Time → Arithmetic Mean (50 km/hr)**
Suppose you drive:

1 hour at 60 km/hr
1 hour at 40 km/hr

Distance traveled:

60 × 1 = 60 km
40 × 1 = 40 km

Total:
Distance = 100 km
Time = 2 hours

Average speed: Speed = Distance / Time

100/2 = 50 km/hr

So here:

Average Speed = (60+40)/2 = 50 km/hr

because the time spent at each speed is equal.

**Case 2: Equal Distance → Harmonic Mean (48 km/hr)**

Now suppose you travel:

60 km at 60 km/hr
60 km at 40 km/hr

Time taken:

60/60 = 1 hour
60/40 = 1.5 hours

Total:

Distance = 120 km
Time = 2.5 hours

Average speed:

120/2.5 = 48 km/hr

So the average speed is:

48 km/hr

not 50 km/hr.

**Why does this happen?**

Because the slower speed (40 km/hr) keeps you on the road longer.

At 60 km/hr → 1 hour
At 40 km/hr → 1.5 hours

**The slower speed contributes more to the total travel time, so it should have more influence on the average. That's exactly what the Harmonic Mean does.**


**Condition	Average Used**
Equal time	Arithmetic Mean
Equal distance	Harmonic Mean

The most important formula in Harmonic Mean

For two speeds a and b over equal distances:

Average Speed = 2ab/(a+b)

Example:

= 2×60×40/(60+40)
= 4800/100
= 48 km/hr

**So your intuition that "50 km/hr can be right" is absolutely correct — but only when the time spent at each speed is equal, not when the distance traveled at each speed is equal. That's the key distinction interviewers look for.**

author: Laxminarayen
title: OLS
body:
OLS - Ordinary Least Squares Method.. 
Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) is a fundamental linear regression method that models the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables by minimizing the sum of squared residuals

author: Laxminarayen
title: Evaluation Metrics
body:
1. SSE - Sum of Squared Errors - (Sum(Actual - Predicted)2) - (square to remove the -ve sign)
2. MSE - Mean(Sum of Square Errors) - On an average what is the error of prediciton for my model?
3. RMSE - Sqrt(MEAN(SSE)) - sqrt(MSE) - Root Mean squared Error..
